title: [recoverability] The mission repositories' restore drill runs on its own, daily: restore-drill --only missions unpacks no transcript (the bundle decrypted in a pipe, never in the clear) and records backup.drilled.missions alone; fsck --full; its unit and timer
prompt:
Spawn, objective 186 [recoverability] (the owner's order of 2026-11-14 18:43: one environment, recovery instead of isolation; restores passed must read 6 of 6, guardrail U1): the mission repositories' restore drill runs on its own, daily, and records its resource alone.

Today the only restore drill of the mission repositories is the combined one (`spawn backup restore-drill`, objective 149), which also restores the transcript archive. Its timer is not installed: it waits for 152 and 154 (what the drill leaves of the transcripts it restores). So the mission repositories have never had a restore proved by a schedule. This objective drills them alone, so they need no transcript rule at all: the drill never unpacks a transcript.

Base: live main 007563ed (the history rewritten 2026-11-15).

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs: restore_drill, run, fetch_bundle, restore_repos, restore_repo, outcomes, fail_both, unrestorable;
- deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill.service (the combined drill's unit, which the new unit follows);
- deploy/backup/README.md, "restore drill".

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup restore-drill --only missions`:
   - From each bundle of the chain it extracts by name only `manifest.json` and the files directly under `repos/`. It never extracts a transcript slice.
   - (R2, rev-f's R1 F1) The bundle is never written in the clear: gpg decrypts the stored ciphertext to a pipe, the drill hashes the stream and feeds it to the decompressor its magic names (zstd, gzip, or none) and on into tar. The stream is read twice: `tar -t` first, whose sha256 must be the record's before anything is extracted; then `tar -x` of the manifest and `repos/*` by name (--no-wildcards, --verbatim-files-from), whose sha256 must be the same. A listing without a manifest is refused before `tar -x` (an empty name list would make tar extract every member). So a run killed at any point (its 1 h limit, MemoryMax, a reboot) leaves only the ciphertext, the list of names and what it has extracted: no transcript in the clear. R1 wrote bundle.raw and bundle.tar, every transcript in them, before extracting by name.
   - It restores every mission source as the combined drill does (clone --mirror of the full bundle, each increment fetched on top, refs set to the newest record's heads; objective 178's commit-map rules for heads made before the rewrite) and compares the refs with live.
   - It records `backup.drilled.missions` only: one record per resource. The transcripts' record is left as it was.
   - It says "restore-drill: --only missions: the mission repositories alone; no transcript unpacked or restored".
   - `--only` takes `missions` alone. Any other value (transcripts, an empty one) is refused with exit 2 and nothing recorded.
   - Without `--only` the drill is as before.
(2) Every restored mirror is checked with `git fsck --full` (every object read whole), in both modes, instead of `--connectivity-only`. The line says "fsck --full clean".
(3) The owner's part:
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-missions.service runs `spawn backup restore-drill --only missions` with the bundle unit's environment (spawn.env), Nice 15, idle I/O, MemoryMax 1G, a 1 h limit; exit 1 (a failed drill) and 2 (one that cannot run) are not retried.
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-missions.timer: daily 05:45 (after the 04:00 bundle and the 05:00 dump drill), Persistent.
   - R2 is only read (GET), with the bundle's own credentials (SPAWN_R2_ENV_FILE). No read-only token is on this host; that one stays on the Mac for a restore on a new machine.
   - deploy/backup/README.md: the schedule row, the install steps (after landing, the lead installs and enables the timer), the usage line.
   - rsi/scenarios/186.sh (new).

What stays as it is: the combined drill and its records; the bundle and its records; every other backup command; the transcript rules (152, 154).

Polled reads: none. The drill runs once a day.

Tests (spawn-cli):
- backup::restore_drill::tests::a_missions_only_drill_extracts_the_manifest_and_the_repository_bundles_alone (new): from a bundle's listing only the manifest and the repository bundles are named, never a transcript slice, a deeper path, a directory or `..`; `--only` takes missions alone.
- The existing restore-drill tests, unchanged.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs (usage), crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (usage). The owner's (186-owner.diff): deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-missions.{service,timer} (new), deploy/backup/README.md, rsi/scenarios/186.sh (new).
Size: fleet 3 files, +408 -48; owner 4 files, +937 -2 (186.sh 878, from 149.sh's world). R2 alone: restore_drill.rs +240 -39 (the pipe: fetch_missions, stream_into_tar and its three helpers, read_manifest split out); 186.sh +89 -4.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/186.sh, black box on its own database, scratch HOME and GNUPGHOME, against 104's local R2 stand-in (149.sh's world: four mission sources, a transcript archive). The bundle and the drill run as their units run them.
(1) The bundle unit's run records backup.bundled (setup).
(2) The missions unit runs `restore-drill --only missions`, and its timer names an OnCalendar. Its run passes (exit 0), says "--only missions", records exactly one backup.drilled.missions {ok true, reason "", the bundle's key and event, 0 mismatches} and no backup.drilled.transcripts, leaves no scratch directory, and changes nothing live.
(3) With --keep, the kept drill directory holds no *.jsonl and no path under transcripts/, but each bundle's manifest and a repository bundle.
(4) Live's main of one source rewritten off the backed-up history: the drill fails (exit 1), missions ok false with a mismatch, still no transcripts record.
(5) --only transcripts and --only '': exit 2, nothing recorded.
(6) (R2) A tar first on PATH kills the drill at its `tar -t`, then (another run) at its `tar -x`: the drill's directory holds no *.jsonl, no bundle.raw or bundle.tar, no file holding a transcript's text, and nothing is recorded.
(7) (R2) The newest bundle's stored bytes replaced by another ciphertext under the same passphrase, its sha256 header left as it was: the drill fails (exit 1) on the decrypted stream's sha256 ("decrypts to sha256"), missions ok false, and a kept drill shows nothing extracted.
(8) No secret (the backup passphrase, the R2 secret key) in a record or the output.
On the base (007563ed with the owner part, the base binary) 186.sh exits 1 at (2): "the drill does not say it drills the missions alone" (the base reads no --only and drills both resources).

Proof (rev-g, sync/obj-186/186-proof.txt), R2 with F2 (rev-f's: start_tar returns a `TarPipes` alias, no clippy allow) on 00689e69 (fleet 156a6570 + 973a48c9, owner e79152ed + bdb545af + 00689e69; range-diff against e8ef649a: only 69cb6e95 -> 973a48c9 changed, one hunk in restore_drill.rs). On 00689e69 itself: build; lists 1106 -> 1107, 0 missing, the same list as e8ef649a's; spawn-cli's backup:: tests (60), fmt --all and clippy -D warnings pass; 186.sh passes twice. On e8ef649a (the same code but for the alias), with the controller 007563ed + the owner part: 186.sh fails on the base at (2), fails on R1 (e79152ed's binary) at (6) (a drill killed at -t left bundle-0/bundle.tar), and passes twice on the candidate; spawn-cli's backup:: tests (60), fmt --all and clippy pass; the kept restore-drill scenarios 104, 114, 149 and 167 pass; lists 1106 -> 1107, 0 missing, 1 new. 9 mutants (mut186.py), each alone with its own binary, in a worktree of their own (never the candidate's): 8 killed by 186.sh (only-ignored, no-refuse, record-both, extract-all, missions-via-files, hash-unchecked, no-early-return, unit-not-only); fsck-connectivity survives: a black box cannot put a corrupt object into a bundle whose sha256 matches its record (git bundle create would refuse it first), so --full is defence in depth and is said so. Not proved by a check: the refusal of a listing with no manifest (the bundler always writes one).

Verified by: the gate runs 186.sh on the candidate. After landing and deploy, the lead installs and enables the missions timer (README). The next morning's backup.drilled.missions is ok, read through the API, and restores passed counts the mission repositories.
